because.label: How to read it
because.value: A club's roster as OOTP lists it (the active roster and the injured list for the major league club, the full roster for an affiliate), with the scouts' grades and this season's lines at that club's level. Show or hide season lines from the table's columns.

because.label: Scouted
because.value: His scouted tools averaged now and at their ceiling, 20–80: your scouts' view, never OOTP's own overall, which your front office can't see. A tool they haven't graded leaves the figure not scouted.

because.label: Season lines
because.value: This season, at this club's level only: a player who has moved between levels has a line at each, and they are never added together.

because.label: OBP
because.value: On-base percentage. The single best simple measure of a hitter avoiding outs.

because.label: OPS
because.value: On-base plus slugging. A quick read of a hitter's whole offense, but unadjusted for league or park.

because.label: BABIP
because.value: Batting average on balls in play. Far from league average (~.300) often signals luck that will regress.

because.label: wOBA
because.value: Weighted on-base average. Like OBP, but each way of reaching base is weighted by how many runs it actually produces. Scaled so league average matches league OBP.

because.label: OPS+
because.value: OPS adjusted for league run environment and ballpark, scaled so 100 = league average. 130 means 30% better than average.

because.label: wRC+
because.value: Weighted Runs Created Plus — the most complete rate stat here. Total offense per plate appearance, park- and league-adjusted, where 100 = league average.

because.label: EV
because.value: Average exit velocity in mph across every batted ball. League average is around 86-87; 92 and up is genuine thump.

because.label: Max EV
because.value: His hardest-hit ball of the season, in mph. A high peak with a modest average means the power is real but intermittent.

because.label: Hard%
because.value: Share of batted balls struck at 95 mph or more. The most stable contact-quality number there is — it settles long before batting average does.

because.label: Brl%
because.value: Share of batted balls hit hard enough, at an angle good enough, to be near-certain damage. The window opens at 98 mph and widens as the ball is hit harder.

because.label: Sweet%
because.value: Share of batted balls launched between 8 and 32 degrees, the angles that produce line drives rather than choppers and popups.

because.label: Sprint
because.value: Measured speed on the bases, averaged across his batted balls — what he actually does, rather than the scouted speed rating.

because.label: xSLG
because.value: What his contact usually produces: every batted ball scored by how balls of that speed and angle actually fared at his level this season.

because.label: SLG±
because.value: Actual slugging on batted balls minus expected. Strongly negative means he has hit the ball well and been robbed; strongly positive means the results have outrun the contact.

because.label: FPCT
because.value: Fielding percentage — putouts plus assists over total chances. It says how often a player handled what he reached, and nothing about how much he reached, so a statue with safe hands can lead the league in it.

because.label: RF/9
because.value: Range factor — putouts plus assists per nine innings. It measures how much a fielder is involved, which is the part fielding percentage misses. Compare it only within a position: a first baseman handles far more chances than a left fielder.

title.hint: Earned run average per nine innings
Walks and hits per inning pitched — baserunners allowed
Strikeout-to-walk ratio. Around 3.0 is excellent command.
Wins Above Replacement, as calculated by OOTP
